reasons.A: Modern plain register with short declaratives, contractions-adjacent ease and a brisk 'That, really, is the heart of it'; none of the passage's long periodic, semicolon-jointed sentences or dry Edwardian irony.
reasons.B: Right period diction and semicolon-linked clauses, and a measured 'It was a jest; but' turn, yet its sentences are more even and less ironically weighted than the passage's accumulating periodic sentences.
reasons.C: Closest movement: long cumulative sentences with piled participial clauses and semicolons, a first-person reflective stance, a concessive 'Of course' turn and a dry ironic close, like the passage; the rhetorical question is a slight overreach.
